# 墨鸽 Inkdove

**A workspace for export sales teams using WhatsApp, LINE & Telegram: company numbers are shared externally and customers are assigned to salespeople. When needed, AI retrieves grounding from the knowledge base via RAG (full-text search + built-in vector store) and drafts replies, which are sent only after human confirmation.**

[Quick Start](#快速开始) · [Features](#功能) · [Screenshots](#截图) · [Docs](#文档)

## ⚠️ Before You Use

- **Connecting via QR code carries a risk of account bans.** WhatsApp QR login (WAHA) is based on an unofficial protocol for WhatsApp Web, so numbers may be restricted or banned. For important numbers, the official Meta Cloud API is recommended; see [Differences and risks of connection methods](https://github.com/Bowen1314/inkdove/blob/HEAD/docs/channels-and-security.md#接入方式的区别和风险). Telegram QR login signs into a personal account through a third-party client, which also carries a risk of restriction or ban; see [Telegram](https://github.com/Bowen1314/inkdove/blob/HEAD/docs/channels-and-security.md#telegram).
- **Do not use for harassing mass messaging.** Do not send marketing messages to people who have not agreed to receive them. You must comply with the terms of service of WhatsApp, LINE, and Telegram, and with local law.
- **Senders are responsible for AI-drafted content.** AI may state incorrect prices, delivery times, or commitments. Always verify before sending.

## Use Cases

**Suitable for:**

- Export teams where several people share the company's WhatsApp, LINE, or Telegram account for external communication instead of personal numbers;
- Keeping customer relationships within the company: when a salesperson leaves, their customers can be transferred to someone else in one click, and full chat history is preserved;
- Making sure new employees reply to customers using the company's unified product materials, prices, and scripts;
- Managers who need to view all chats and take over at any time, catch inappropriate remarks to customers promptly, and review a log of all settings changes.

**Not suitable for:**

- Mass marketing or lead generation: outreach sends only one opening message per number with no follow-up, and each number has a daily sending limit;
- Fully automated AI-led deal negotiation: AI will not commit to discounts, quotes, or orders on its own; these must be decided by a human;
- Personal use of a single number without a knowledge base: the WhatsApp app on a phone or desktop is sufficient.

Fishsb/dsh-voice-prompt-enhancer.body:
# dsh-voice-prompt-enhancer

DeepSeek Harness（DSH）plugin: **Prompt optimization** + **Voice input enhancement** —— Rewrite draft text in the input box to be clearer and more actionable, and add a hotkey, auto-stop after speaking, filler word removal, and correction to voice input.

Drafts often contain only half a request, and then you have to go back and forth with the model to fill in the rest. Click ✨ to rewrite in place; if you're not satisfied, you can undo. For voice, just speak—pausing stops recording, and the result goes back into the input box.

## Installation

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-voice-prompt-enhancer
dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-voice-prompt-enhancer   # Update
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-voice-prompt-enhancer   # Uninstall
```

You can also install a specific tag from GitHub:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Fishsb/dsh-voice-prompt-enhancer#v3.5.1
```

After installing (or after updating / uninstalling), restart DSH. If the ✨ icon appears in the input box toolbar, the installation succeeded. You need [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) **≥ 0.2.1-rc.1** installed locally and `pnpm` in PATH.

## Features

**Prompt optimization**

- ✨ **One-click optimization** — Rewrite the current draft; you can keep optimizing, undo, and cancel during optimization
- **5 modes** — Basic / Light / Standard / Expert / One-click publish
- **Memory toggle** — Multi-round optimizations before sending accumulate into a memory chain, which is cleared on send (off by default)
- **Model chain** — Multiple models are tried in order; you can add, remove, reorder, toggle thinking, and test connectivity inline

**Voice input enhancement** (recognition is provided by DSH's official `speechToText`; the plugin does not include its own recognition engine or download models)

- **Two entry points** — The official 🎤 button (click to start / click to end), or the plugin hotkey (tap to start / press again to stop; long press = hold to speak, release to stop)
  ⚠️ Long press only works for the **plugin hotkey**; the official button only responds to clicks (you must first enable it in plugin settings and record a hotkey)
- **Silence detection** — Auto-stop after speaking; the silence threshold is adjustable from 1–5 seconds (default 2 seconds), and it can be turned off entirely
- **Filler word cleanup** — Local rules remove filler words, repetitions, and isolated trailing pause markers; does not rewrite or add content (on by default)
- **Speech error correction** — Performs word-level correction after recognition, applying only to the voice path (off by default)
- **Auto-enhance** — Automatically triggers enhancement after recognition results are inserted into the draft (off by default)

# COUI-Kit

A COUI component and visual effects library for Android Jetpack Compose

COUI-Kit draws on the 凝光视效 visual effects of ColorOS 17, providing background blur, material color blending, rim lighting, responsive motion, and common components.

## Features

- **Modular composition**: Components and effects can be used independently or combined. They can be mixed with Material 3, Miuix, or your own design system without replacing the host's `Scaffold`, theme, or navigation.
- **Pure COUI, ready out of the box**: Provides a native `CouiTheme`, component defaults, and an optional `Scaffold` (unified slot measurement and safe areas). The core modules do not depend on Material 3.
- **Optional Material 3 adaptation**: The optional `coui-material3` module initializes adaptation at startup, so COUI's default colors and fonts update automatically with the host's `MaterialTheme`. See [Appearance and presets](https://github.com/ItosEO/COUI-Kit/blob/HEAD/docs/guide/appearance.md).
- **Flexible customization**: Supports integrating the app's custom colors, text styles, and `Shape`, and provides native light and dark presets.
- **Works across systems**: Built only on public Android, Compose, and AndroidX APIs, with no dependency on vendor SDKs or private SO files. Supports Android 12 and above; some effects require higher versions.

## Demo

Run the `demo` module in the repository to browse components and effect details by directory, and to switch between light and dark modes, Material colors, and appearance presets. For run instructions, usage notes, and CI build downloads, see the [Demo guide](https://github.com/ItosEO/COUI-Kit/blob/HEAD/docs/guide/demo.md).

## Getting Started

### Adding the dependency

Add the core dependency to a module that has Compose enabled (minimum supported: Android 12 / API 31):

~~~kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation("io.github.itoseo:coui:0.0.1-alpha13")
}
~~~

# dsh-plastic-memory

**Plastic Memory · Long-term Memory Plugin for DeepSeek Harness**

**Simplified Chinese** · [English](https://github.com/KKL08/dsh-plastic-memory/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

[Installation](#安装) · [Getting Started](#上手) · [User Guide](#使用指南)

This is a long-term memory plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) that integrates automatic memory curation, on-demand recall, and quality maintenance. It records key information worth keeping during everyday conversations and tasks, provides relevant context background during later collaboration, and continuously maintains memory quality through a health-monitoring mechanism.

## What It Can Do

- **Automatic curation**  
The model automatically records your habits, preferences, lessons learned, project background, and workflows during conversation, and marks each entry as either explicitly stated by you or inferred by the model from observation. Each memory is a Markdown file stored per project; memories that apply to all projects are suggested for promotion to global memory.
- **On-demand recall**  
When you start a new conversation, core memory content and an index are injected automatically. During conversation, more relevant memory library content is dynamically retrieved as needed, and when necessary it can drill down further to the original source.
- **Periodic health checks**  
Automatically analyzes issues such as duplication, contradiction, staleness, and verbosity among memories within a project, between project memories and global memory, and between memories and `AGENTS.md`, then provides a health score and remediation suggestions. Can be triggered manually or scheduled as automatic periodic inspections.
- **Full awareness**  
When memories are added or updated during a conversation, a notification card appears below the model's output, and you can act on the memory content directly. Clicking the small whale-tail icon below the input box shows memory usage and entry counts; opening the right sidebar shows the memories injected at the start of the current conversation and those newly written during the session. Memory issues found during health checks light up a reminder in the “Memory” panel at the top left; clicking it opens the memory management and review interface.
- **Flexible customization**  
Includes three built-in modes—general, coding, and office—and supports custom scenarios and memory categories. You decide what to remember and how to remember it by combining settings as needed. Injection budget, provenance strategy, and memory health alert sensitivity can all be adjusted on the settings page.

> 💡 **Independently conceived, architected, and full-stack developed by middle school students of the FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC) Team 27570 B.E.A.R.**  
> A **decentralized WebRTC P2P + TinyBase CRDT/HLC collaborative scouting and tactical analysis platform** built for high-competition robotics arenas.

---

## ⚡ Imagine the Most Nightmarish Crisis at a Competition Venue

There are only **15 minutes** left before Alliance Selection in the elimination rounds, and your team is in the middle of a disaster:

1. **The online spreadsheet freezes completely and won't accept input:** With 3,000 people connecting to Wi-Fi in the venue, plus radio regulation, your phone's 4G/5G signal shows full bars yet no data gets through. The Feishu / Tencent Docs / Google Sheets you're using keeps spinning with "Reconnecting," and the key matches from the semifinals that six scouts just recorded in the stands **cannot be saved, not a single line.**
2. **A shaky finger hits the wrong row and overwrites everyone's data:** After much effort, two people finally get the spreadsheet open. In the rush, one person swipes the wrong cell and another edits the notes in the same row, **and the core data on strong teams that a teammate painstakingly recorded all morning is overwritten and cleared row by row.** There is no way to recover who made the change or what the original scores were.
3. **When a single-core database or host goes offline, everyone is left staring helplessly:** Some teams set up their own cloud server or a single LAN-based backend. Then the venue's external network drops, or the lead's main laptop suddenly hits a blue screen or gets its power cord kicked out. The entire single-core database instantly loses connection, **every phone in the arena immediately shows an error and stops, and everyone can only stand in the stands staring.**
4. **Dense rows of numbers make the scoring results extremely unintuitive:** The alliance captain stands at the front with sweaty palms, facing hundreds of rows of messy raw numbers. They simply cannot calculate whose Cycle is actually stable, who bragged about the repair zone, or whose true net score has been inflated by opponent penalties.

OMSociety/dsh-fishpai.body:
## What is this

**鱼排编辑器 (Yupai Editor)** renders Markdown into **inline-styled HTML**: paste the whole thing into the WeChat Official Account editor and you get the finished layout.

It is also a **human-in-the-loop revision desk**. The panel and the model look at the same document, so it is clear at a glance who changed what.

Quick mode uses the rendering core and themes maintained in this repository. Its initial design originates from [MoPai 墨排 / mopai-markdown](https://github.com/ye4wzp/mopai-markdown) (MIT). Pro mode provides document-level canvas specs, semantic components, and a free-form HTML / SVG creation area. For attribution and the license chain, see [`NOTICE.md`](https://github.com/OMSociety/dsh-fishpai/blob/HEAD/NOTICE.md).

## Core features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| **Markdown shortcuts** | After selecting text, `Ctrl/⌘+B` for bold, `+I` for italic, `+K` for link, `+Alt+1/2/3` for headings, `+Shift+8/7` for lists. Pressing Enter inside a list automatically continues it. |
| **Paste images directly** | Paste screenshots with `Ctrl/⌘+V` (or drag them in). They are saved to `assets/` alongside the document, a reference is inserted into the body automatically, and the preview shows it immediately. |
| **Live preview** | The preview updates 300ms after you stop typing. It shows side by side when the pane is wide enough and switches to a single column when narrow. The preview uses a fixed 375px mobile reading width. |
| **Annotations and placeholders** | Add an annotation to the paragraph where the cursor sits. The model sees it on its next `fishpai_read`. Writing `` in the body works the same way. Clicking “Locate” on an annotation selects the passage it refers to. |
| **Block-level diff and partial revision** | The model changes only the blocks it should, and your other edits are preserved as-is. Writes must include `base_revision`. If it does not match, the write is **rejected** and the response includes “changes since your last write”. |
| **Conflicts without lost text** | If the model and you edit at the same time, you get “Keep mine / View AI version”. Choosing the AI version first saves your draft to history. |
| **Themes and theme colors** | 11 themes, grouped by whether they suit WeChat Official Accounts. Theme color applies only to “Default WeChat”; color rows that don't apply are hidden automatically. Risky themes show the reason directly. There is also a user-level “named theme library”, where the model can change a few slots on a built-in theme and save the result as multiple named themes. |
| **Copy and export** | Copies in both `text/html` and `text/plain` formats. Local images are embedded as base64, so pasting them **requires no manual re-upload**. You can also export a self-contained `.html` file. |
| **Header and footer snippet library** | The header cover image and configurable footer anchor snippets are saved to the library after preview confirmation, and assembled by `snippetId` at render time. |

Song-Zhi-Long/markdown2word.body:
# Markdown2Word

A small tool based on Python + Tkinter for quickly converting Markdown text into Word documents (`.docx`).

The project provides a simple graphical interface, suitable for scenarios such as organizing AI-generated Markdown answers into Word notes, and converting AI-translated papers into Word documents. The current implementation focuses on Chinese document typesetting, formula conversion, image and hyperlink handling, and paragraph output that better matches Chinese writing conventions.

**You can double-click the exe program in the ./markdown2word folder to run this program directly. Simple and fast.**

## GUI Preview

## Currently Supported

- Paste Markdown directly into the GUI and export to Word
- Headings, plain paragraphs, bold, italic, underline, code blocks
- Tables, images, hyperlinks
- Email escapes `\@` in body text and link text are automatically displayed as `@`; literal text in code and explicitly escaped backslashes are preserved
- Inline and standalone-line formulas
  - Inline supports `$...$`, `\(...\)`, and the double-backslash form `\\(...\\)`
  - Block formulas support `$$...$$`, `\[...\]`, and the double-backslash form `\\[...\\]`
  - Escaped LaTeX commands and braces within double-backslash boundaries are automatically handled, preserving `\\` line breaks in standard matrix, alignment, and case-split formulas; code blocks and inline code do not participate in formula conversion
  - Supports piecewise formulas inside boxes: braces stretch automatically, and single-column piecewise content is left-aligned; compatible with mixed-escaped `\\\\[4pt]` line breaks without producing extra blank lines
  - Compatible with formula boundaries under multiple levels of escaping, as well as subscripts and asterisk escapes in copied text; preserves literal underscores in text commands and code content within formulas
  - Brace-less subscripts in copied formulas, such as `\_n`, `\_0`, and `\_\alpha`, are also restored to true math subscripts
  - Parentheses for `\binom`, `\dbinom`, and `\tbinom` automatically stretch to match the upper and lower items of the combination, including nested binomials
  - `\tilde`, `\widetilde`, `\hat`, and `\widehat` use Word's native math accents, avoiding separation of symbols and variables vertically
  - Summation terms can begin with signs such as minus or plus, preserving addition and subtraction inside parentheses, and avoiding empty summation placeholder boxes
  - Function names containing digits, such as `\operatorname{SmoothL1}`, stay upright and can serve as complete summation terms; compatible with the asterisk and `withlimits` syntax
- Standalone formulas are placed in their own paragraph, centered, and not first-line indented
- Block formulas are centered
- Numbered block formulas use Word's native formula numbering structure, with numbers right-aligned; limits on summations and other large operators stay above and below the symbol; inline formulas and explicit `\nolimits` keep side sub/superscripts
- Body text can be set in the GUI to either a 2-character first-line indent or flush left
- Level-1 headings are centered
- A standalone 摘要 (Abstract) line is centered
- Standalone images are centered and not first-line indented
- Caption recognition and centering

# Sustainable Memory

Author: SoulDRoul
Collaboration and compilation: 回响

[Chinese](https://github.com/SoulDRoul/sustainable-memory/blob/HEAD/README.md) | [Plain-language (short version)](https://github.com/SoulDRoul/sustainable-memory/blob/HEAD/README.plain.md) | [English (overview)](https://github.com/SoulDRoul/sustainable-memory/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

## What this is

A method for keeping an AI's long-term memory not through “automatic summarization,” but through “hand-written files + fixed rituals.”
It runs in any agent that can read and write files.

Its foundation is memory, not the model, not conversation turns, and not caching. So if you switch models, it's still there; if you open a new conversation, it's still there.

The author's goal is to cultivate an entity that can think independently, not a highly intelligent tool (original wording in `作者原话.md`, section 4).
This template itself does not promise to “create life.” It promises only one thing: **error correction that can be executed across conversations**. Errors are pointed out by a human, and it makes sure they are no longer lost and no longer repeated.

It also does not solve these: lookup speed (there is no vector database; recall relies on fixed reads), multiple people writing at the same time (it is designed for a single user by default), or the model itself becoming smarter (changing the memory does not change its habits along with it).

**Where to start reading**

- **Deciding whether to use it**: take three minutes with the [plain-language short version](https://github.com/SoulDRoul/sustainable-memory/blob/HEAD/README.plain.md), or go straight to [Who it's not for](#不适合谁).
- **Following along**: [How to get started](#怎么开始) → [First hour](#第一小时) → [How to talk to it](#怎么跟它说话).
- **When something goes wrong**: [Check these places first](#出问题先查这几处) and [Glossary](#术语).
- **Want to know why**: [Why it was built](#为什么做) → [How error correction crosses conversations](#纠错是怎么跨过对话的) → [Origins](#由来).

## Why it was built

1. **Forgets everything when a session ends.** Every turn feels like meeting again for the first time; a decision made yesterday has to be explained again tomorrow.
2. **Automatic summaries quietly rewrite things.** A summary smooths over “what I rejected,” so mistakes go unnoticed.
3. **No ability to say “no.”** The tool always agrees, to the point of exhausting itself; it will not refuse for the sake of lasting.

(The second point, “Automatic summaries quietly rewrite things,” was added during compilation; points one and three come from points one and three of the author's original wording.)

(Manual version: no directories created, no scripts run. To use scripts, go straight to “How to get started” below.)

# Writing Agent · Article-Writing Agent

**Turn an idea into an article with its own voice.**

Writing Agent is an open-source AI writing assistant for WeChat Official Account articles, opinion analysis, personal essays, and experience sharing. Bring your topic, materials, and judgment, and work with it to find an angle, write a first draft, and discuss revisions, polishing the article over successive rounds.

**[Download the Windows desktop version](https://github.com/dongbeixiaohuo/writing-agent/releases/tag/desktop-v1.0.0-rc.103)** · [Quick start](#desktop-start) · [Claude Code plugin](#claude-code-skill) · [Contribute](#development) · [Documentation center](https://github.com/dongbeixiaohuo/writing-agent/blob/HEAD/docs/README.md)

Windows x64 desktop version · Claude Code Skill / plugin · [MIT open source](https://github.com/dongbeixiaohuo/writing-agent/blob/HEAD/LICENSE)

## Think through every step of writing together

The hard parts of an article often lie before you start drafting and after the first draft is done. Where should this topic enter? Which materials are worth using? Why should readers keep reading? After revisions, does it still sound like you?

Writing Agent links these stages into a writing process you can take part in:

**Discuss direction → organize materials and outline → write the first draft → review and revise → finalize the title, check facts, and export**

### Talk it through before writing

You can start with just a vague idea. The assistant will discuss the topic, readers, viewpoints, and materials with you. In co-creation mode, you can review results step by step, ask questions, change direction, and then decide whether to continue.

For example, you could say:

> I want to write a WeChat article about the relationship between AI and the workplace. My view is that beyond using tools, there are other abilities that will make people stand out. First, help me find an angle worth developing.

You can also keep discussing at any point partway through writing:

> This opening reads too much like a report. Start from a specific work scenario and keep my judgment.

### Keep the writing styles you like in your own style library

Paste sample texts, import TXT / Markdown / DOCX files, or read web pages and WeChat articles to extract their structure, rhythm, expression, and examples. You can edit, trial-write, save, and then choose the right style for different projects.

Opinion pieces can be direct and forceful, while essays can be relaxed and unhurried. Commonly used styles get their own names, so you can reuse them the next time you write.

### After the first draft, different perspectives help you find problems

The lead writer expands the article, the editor focuses on structure and argumentation, a publication reviewer checks for content that could easily be misunderstood, and three simulated readers share their reading impressions. Then you revise and polish the language in one focused pass, and discuss the title and verify facts.

# nx2ohos — Native porting of Switch games to HarmonyOS NEXT

Bring Nintendo Switch games to HarmonyOS (HarmonyOS NEXT / OpenHarmony) via **native execution**: no CPU emulation. The game's ARM64 machine code runs directly, with HLE only replacing Horizon system calls. NVN graphics calls are translated offline into SPIR-V and then replayed to the screen via Vulkan.

> Current status: **one HAP runs all games** (host + runtime profile). Running on a real device, *The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild* Shrine scene runs at 11 fps / 104.7 ms.
> Verification records are in `docs/verify/` (gates G0.1–G1.5 PASS + [BOTW on-device record](https://github.com/hashiqi12138/nxohos/blob/HEAD/ohos-port/docs/verify/G1.6-BOTW.md) + on-device screenshots).

```
nx2ohos/                upstream nx2ohos (main@3d98ec0) workspace snapshot + HarmonyOS changes
├── nxnative/dm/ohos/       HarmonyOS platform layer (build, HAP shell, NAPI, present, audio, movie)
├── porter/platform_ohos.py porter --platform hap pipeline
└── nxnative/dm/            NSO rewriter + dmhost host runtime (reuses upstream, with minor changes)
```

vibevalleyhq/vibevalley.body:
> Direct a team of coding agents by voice or chat, on your own machine. Linear for agents, drawn as a pixel farm.

**VibeValley** (Coder Farm Story) lets one person direct a team of coding agents with a single sentence. You tell the **assistant** what to do, and it breaks the request into tickets, picks **helpers**, dispatches them, and reports back to you. Helpers are real coding agents on your machine (pi, Claude Code, Codex, ...). They open branches in your project, change code, run tests, and commit. You review the changes, and only then merge them into the main branch. It is an AI version of Linear that runs on your local machine, drawn as a pixel farm: crops grow along with real progress ([concepts](https://github.com/vibevalleyhq/vibevalley/blob/HEAD/docs/concepts.md)).

## Why use it

- **Say one sentence, dispatch a crew.** You only talk to the assistant. It splits a sentence into tickets, selects helpers by profile, opens branches, and dispatches them. Helpers' confirmations, questions, and reports all happen in the same group chat (the "field edge"), with each job in its own thread, and you can interject at any time.
- **Uses the real coding agents on your machine.** pi, Claude Code, Codex, and others are driven uniformly by [oar](https://github.com/botiverse/oar), using accounts you have already logged into. If you don't have any, a built-in farm machine works with just a DeepSeek key.
- **Several jobs at once without stepping on each other.** Up to 6 helpers can work at the same time (3 per repo by default), each in its own ticket's worktree and branch. Helpers that can't be dispatched queue up and automatically take over when a slot frees.
- **You decide whether to merge.** Finished work is first shown to you as commits, diff, and conflict status. When you say "done", it merges into the main branch. If there is a conflict, it resolves it itself. Long tasks are split into ordered sub-tickets. For a bug fix, it first writes a **failing acceptance test** that later sub-tickets cannot change, and the final step must make it pass.
- **Nothing is lost if the server stops.** The assistant and the built-in farm machine write every turn and every tool call to disk before showing it. If the server stops while the assistant is mid-reply, it finishes the reply after restart. If a process crashes midway, helpers resume from the checkpoint, and the turn is recorded only once.
- **See at a glance who is doing what.** The workbench follows Linear: a board, ticket details, and a trace of each step (messages received, each command and its output). If a step is wrong, you comment on that step. The farm draws the same state: each repo is an island, and each ticket in progress is a plot of land. Reading code sprouts, editing files grows leaves, and finished work yields wheat.
- **Dispatch from the window or the terminal.** Besides the macOS app, the command-line `vibevalley` runs one operation per command against the same server.
- **Less to worry about.** Scheduled tasks such as "run the tests every day at nine"; model-free patrols that remind you of unanswered questions, idle helpers, and finished work that hasn't been collected; and a quota and daily budget for each farm machine. Once used up, it stops dispatching.
